title: The stellar lifecycle in a nearby spiral
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 5134, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 5134 · constellation Virgo · about 65 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #25 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A tilted spiral galaxy glows faintly blue with the light of its many stars, while bright red strands of dust swirl around a blue-white core and gather in places into orange clumps. This is NGC 5134, about 65 million light-years away in Virgo, captured by two of Webb's instruments working together.

The light in this picture left the galaxy soon after Tyrannosaurus rex went extinct, yet NGC 5134 counts as fairly close for a galaxy, so Webb can resolve fine detail in its tightly wound arms. The mid-infrared instrument, MIRI, traces warm dust in the gas clouds, some of it made of carbon-ring molecules called polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The near-infrared camera, NIRCam, records light mostly from stars and star clusters.

Together they show a galaxy in constant give and take. Stars form in clouds along the arms, using up gas, and dying stars return some of it, either in supernova explosions or more gently as red giants shed their outer layers.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.16 x 2.15 arcminutes) and distance (65 million light years), the frame spans roughly 41,000 × 41,000 light-years. Its light set out about 65 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam and MIRI combined near- and mid-infrared light: blue, cyan and green show near-infrared starlight, orange traces PAH dust emission and red shows mid-infrared glow from warm dust.
understand.eye: All of these wavelengths are infrared and invisible to the human eye.

explore: Only stars above about eight times the Sun's mass end as supernovae, which can spread material across hundreds of light-years. The data come from observing programme #3707, which aims to study 55 nearby galaxies that are actively forming stars. Learning from close galaxies like this helps astronomers interpret distant ones, like the tiny background galaxies here that are barely more than points of light.
alt: A tilted spiral galaxy with a blue-white core and a faint blue disc, laced with swirling red dust strands and orange clumps, with tiny distant galaxies in the background.
